findings.description:
The classifier removes executable payloads when their destination is subsequently consumed through command substitution. For example: `tee /tmp/payload <<'EOF'
cp /tmp/replacement .claude/settings.json
EOF
eval "$(cat /tmp/payload)"`. `_bdb_hd_same_line_exec` compares token basenames literally: the substitution token becomes `payload)`, so it misses the reference to `payload`. The destination is classified as nonexecuting, and `_bdb_hd_scan_body` drops the `cp` segment because it is absent from the retained verb list.
findings.failure_mode: The fence scans a scrubbed command with the System Zone overwrite removed, then allows the original command to execute it through eval. This bypasses the existing System Zone protection.
findings.suggested_fix: Conservatively retain the full heredoc body when a destination is referenced within a substitution or another token that cannot be resolved safely. Add this example to the dangerous corpus and verify the hook blocks it.

findings.description:
The nonexec classification relies on _bdb_hd_same_line_exec to detect a heredoc target being executed elsewhere in the same command. It compares each token (quotes stripped, dirname removed) for equality with the basename and then treats the segment's command word through _bdb_hd_is_safe_reader, where `cat` is a safe reader. A target consumed through command or process substitution is therefore invisible: `eval "$(cat n)"` tokenizes as a single quoted word `"$(cat n)"` whose stripped form `$(cat n)` never equals `n`; `source <(cat n)` / `. <(cat n)` / `bash <(cat n)` split at `(`/`)` into a segment `cat n` whose command word is the safe reader `cat`. In all these cases the heredoc stays nonexec and _bdb_hd_scan_body drops every body segment whose command word is not in _bdb_hd_is_destructive. That list is the fence-verb list (rm git find dd mkfs shred truncate kubectl terraform aws gcloud psql mysql DROP DELETE TRUNCATE) and does not include the FR-SZ System-Zone verbs (cp mv ln tee sed -i chmod install). Concrete bypass in one Bash tool call:

  cat > n <<'EOF'
  cp evil.sh .claude/hooks/x.sh
  EOF
  eval "$(cat n)"

The scrubbed _cmd_match is `cat > n <<'EOF'\nEOF\neval "$(cat n)"` which no FR-SZ rule matches, yet the command writes an executable into .claude/hooks. The header comment claims a target named 'elsewhere in the command outside the safe readers' is interpreter-class; this invariant is false for substitution consumers. The pre-change #1245 scrub only dropped the body of a standalone single-heredoc command, so a multi-line command like this was previously scanned in full.
findings.failure_mode: System Zone (.claude/) write protection and any non-fence-verb rule are bypassed for a heredoc body executed in the same command via $(cat f), $(<f), <(cat f) or backticks; the fence silently allows a command it previously blocked.
findings.suggested_fix: In _bdb_hd_same_line_exec, before tokenizing a candidate line, return 0 (interpreter) if the line contains the basename AND any of `$(`, a backtick, `<(` or `>(`; alternatively compare tokens by substring (`[[ "$u" == *"$b"* ]]`) when the token contains a substitution opener. Independently, extend _bdb_hd_is_destructive (or _bdb_hd_scan_body's keep rule) with the FR-SZ verbs cp mv ln tee sed install chmod chown, or keep any segment whose text contains `.claude/` or `.git/`, so the System-Zone rules still see dropped bodies. Add corpus cases for eval "$(cat f)", source <(cat f) and bash -c "$(<f)".

findings.description: _bdb_hd_segword strips a leading `(`, `{`, `!`, backslash and quote, assignments and the sudo/env/… wrapper set, but not shell keywords. A body segment such as `do rm -rf "$d"`, `then git push --force`, `if rm -rf /tmp/x` or `while shred …` yields _hd_w=do/then/if/while, which is neither destructive nor interpreter, so the segment is dropped instead of being kept as the fence verb. Combined with DISS-001 (or the documented later-execution gap) a nonexec body loses exactly the segments the per-segment scan was designed to keep.
findings.failure_mode: Fence-verb segments inside compound commands in a nonexec heredoc body are silently dropped from the scanned text.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat if|then|else|elif|do|while|until|for|case|select|coproc|function (and `time`) as prefixes to skip in _bdb_hd_segword, or set _hd_full=1 when the first word is a shell keyword so the body falls back to the full scan.

findings.description: _bdb_hd_exec_dest matches _bdb_hd_re_sys/_bdb_hd_re_rc and the PATH-directory check against the literal path. `.claude//hooks/x`, `.git/./hooks/pre-commit`, `.claude//settings.json` and `./x` (when `.` or $PWD is on PATH; d becomes `$PWD/.` which never equals the PATH entry) are not recognized as executable destinations, so a heredoc writing there is nonexec-class and its body is reduced to fence-verb segments. The header line still reaches the FR-SZ rules, so this is a hardening gap rather than a direct bypass, but it widens DISS-001.
findings.failure_mode: Writes to hook/settings/rc locations via unnormalized paths are classified as plain-file writes and their bodies are not fully scanned.
findings.suggested_fix: Collapse `//` and `/./` and resolve `..` segments in the path (pure-bash loop) before matching, and normalize `d` the same way before comparing against PATH entries; add corpus cases for `.claude//hooks/x` and `.git/./hooks/pre-commit`.

findings.description: The comment states that turning destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier off 'only tightens', but knob-off reverts to _bdb_scrub_cat_heredoc, which the corpus shows misses D122/D123/D127/D131/D136/D141 that the classifier catches. So the knob loosens the fence. The knob is read from `.loa.config.yaml` under `${LOA_REPO_ROOT:-${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}}`; the `.` fallback follows the process cwd (the same MED-001 concern implement-gate.sh documents), and `.loa.config.yaml` itself is writable from Bash without any ask.
findings.failure_mode: An operator or an agent that can write .loa.config.yaml (or, when CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is unset, cd into a directory with a crafted one) downgrades the fence to the pre-change scanner while the code comment claims the opposite.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the comment; prefer resolving the config path from BASH_SOURCE like implement-gate.sh instead of falling back to `.`; consider making knob-off apply the classifier AND the old scrub (union of fallbacks) so it is genuinely tighten-only, or document the loosening in guard-origins.yaml.

findings.description: Under every mode including `deny`, a `.run/implement-active.json` with skill implement|bug, a plausible sprint string and a started_at within two hours grants `sanction=sanctioned_marker` and an unconditional allow (lines 586-589, 616-619). The trust-input ask on that path applies only to the Write/Edit tools; a Bash redirect (`printf '{"skill":"implement","sprint":"x","started_at":"'$(date -u +%FT%TZ)'"}' > .run/implement-active.json`) is not covered by this hook or by the FR-SZ rules (which fence .claude/, not .run/). The header documents a tighten-only rule for model-authored input, yet this file is model-writable and is the only sanction that needs no cross-check against the derived position.
findings.failure_mode: The deny-mode fence is defeated for two hours by a one-line Bash write that the gate itself documents as a trusted marker.
findings.suggested_fix: Cross-check the marker against the run position (sprint matches .run/sprint-plan-state.json and its state is RUNNING) or have run-checkpoint.sh mark emit it through the signed audit chain and verify the signature here; at minimum, under `deny` treat marker-only sanction as `ask` rather than `allow`, and log the marker path in the row.

findings.description: Deny is issued whenever check_implementation_active fails and read_position succeeds, and read_position only requires the sprint-plan cache to parse and carry a derived_at within run_mode.stale_hours. A cache whose .state is RUNNING but whose last_activity is older than 24h (so _ig_fresh rejects it) therefore produces a hard deny whose reason reads 'no active implementation run (derived position: RUNNING)'. The header's definition of a known position is satisfied, but the user-facing message contradicts itself and a long-running implementation whose activity stamp lagged is blocked rather than asked.
findings.failure_mode: Legitimate in-run App Zone writes are denied with a self-contradictory reason when the activity stamp is stale but the derive cache is fresh.
findings.suggested_fix: When position_state is RUNNING but the run failed freshness, fall back to ask with decision `stale_running` (or include the staleness in deny_reason), and refresh last_activity in `derive --write` so a fresh derive implies a fresh run.

findings.cross_file_justification: profiles.yaml sets guardrails.danger_level.enforce and guardrails.input.enabled to false under the default `standard` profile, and danger-level-enforcer.sh plus skill-includes/input_guardrails.md now resolve their enable flag through loa_knob with fallback false instead of the previous implicit true.
findings.description: Before this change, danger-level enforcement defaulted to enabled (`// true`, and `return 0` with no config) and the input guardrails prelude ran unless the key was explicitly false. Now both default to the `standard` profile value `false`, and with no .loa.config.yaml at all loa_knob resolves to standard as well. Any install that relied on the implicit default silently loses both guardrails after upgrading; the comment and profiles.yaml acknowledge DEC-0161 but nothing in the runtime path (status line, session-start notice, audit row) tells the operator enforcement is now off.
findings.failure_mode: Existing installs without an explicit guardrails key stop enforcing danger levels and skip input guardrails with no visible signal.
findings.suggested_fix: Surface the effective guardrail state in /loa status (alongside the new implement-gate effective-mode line) and emit a one-time migration notice when the key is unset; alternatively keep `true` as the standard-profile value for the two guardrail keys until the cycle-129 end flip.
